topics: 🙏 Preparing for Prayer — 'Prepare to greet your God, Israel' and how the Sages dressed for the Amida
📖 Torah Study vs. Prayer — Rava's rebuke of Rav Hamnuna and Rabbi Zeira's rebuke of Rabbi Yirmeya
⏰ The Court Day — when a trial begins, how long judges may sit, and the baraita on the hours of eating
🛁 Praying in the Bathhouse — the three rooms and where prayer, greeting, and tefillin are permitted
🎁 The Gift of Shabbat — 'a good gift in My treasure house,' and why a giver must inform the recipient
👨‍👦 Rav's Life Advice — never favor one child, and always dwell in a newly-settled town

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Standing Before God, Sitting in Judgment
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 10a–10b
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens mid-discussion of preparing oneself with dignity before prayer, quoting Amos: 'Prepare to greet your God, Israel.' From there the Gemara moves, by association, through a set of independent teachings: whether Torah study may be interrupted for prayer, when a court session formally begins and how long judges may sit before eating, where in a bathhouse one may pray or greet a friend, and why a gift-giver — God included, with the gift of Shabbat — must inform the recipient that a gift has been given. The daf closes with practical wisdom from Rav about family and where to live.

slides.title: ⏰ Court in Session: From Opening to the Judges' Meal
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yirmeya, Rabbi Yona, Rav Sheshet, and a baraita on daily eating times
rows: Rabbi Yirmeya: from when the judges wrap themselves in their prayer shawls. Rabbi Yona: from when the litigants begin to plead — not a real dispute, since it depends on whether the court was already sitting
Rav Sheshet: until mealtime, since 'your ministers eat... in strength and not in drunkenness' (Ecclesiastes 10:16–17) — i.e. only after Torah and judgment
1st hour: Ludim (ravenous cannibals); 2nd: robbers; 3rd: heirs; 4th: all people; 5th: workers; 6th: Torah scholars, who study until court adjourns

callout.label: One true hour:
callout.text: Rav Ḥiyya bar Rav from Difti taught: 'the people stood over Moses from the morning until the evening' (Exodus 18:13) cannot mean Moses judged all day — his own Torah study needed time. Rather, any judge who renders one truthful judgment, even for a single hour, is considered a partner with God in the work of Creation (Genesis 1:5, 'evening and morning, one day').

slides.title: 📖 Torah Study or Prayer — Which Takes Priority?
slides.subtitle: Two sages, each criticized for the opposite excess

lines.speaker: Rava
lines.text: Watching Rav Hamnuna prolong his prayer: 'They abandon eternal life — Torah study — and occupy themselves with temporal life!'

lines.speaker: Defense
lines.text: Rav Hamnuna held that the time for prayer is distinct from the time for Torah; one is not at the expense of the other.

lines.speaker: R' Yirmeya
lines.text: Sitting before Rabbi Zeira engaged in halakha, he hurried to finish as the time for prayer approached.

lines.speaker: R' Zeira
lines.text: Applied to him: מֵסִיר אׇזְנוֹ מִשְּׁמוֹעַ תּוֹרָה גַּם תְּפִלָּתוֹ תּוֹעֵבָה — 'One who turns his ear from hearing Torah, his prayer too is an abomination' (Proverbs 28:9).

callout.label: Tension:
callout.text: The Gemara juxtaposes both incidents without resolving them — a warning against excess in either direction.

slides.title: 🛁 Where in the Bathhouse May One Pray?
slides.subtitle: Rav Adda bar Ahava's ruling, tested against a Tosefta's three rooms

nodes.content: ❓ Rav Adda bar Ahava: a person may, ab initio, recite his prayer in the bathhouse
📜 A Tosefta describes a Roman bathhouse in three rooms

columns.label: Outer room
columns.content: People stand dressed — Torah reading, prayer, greeting, and tefillin all permitted

columns.label: Middle room
columns.content: People stand both naked and dressed — greeting permitted; no prayer or reading; tefillin not removed but not donned anew

columns.label: Inner room
columns.content: People stand naked — nothing permitted; tefillin must be removed

nodes.content: ✅ Resolved: Rav Adda meant only an empty, new bathhouse never yet used for bathing — even there, 'shalom' stays forbidden, since it is one of God's own names (Judges 6:24)

slides.title: 🎁 A Good Gift Locked Away — and Shabbat Is Its Name
slides.subtitle: Why a giver must announce a gift
slides.hebrewSource: מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לִי בְּבֵית גְּנָזַי וְשַׁבָּת שְׁמָהּ, וַאֲנִי מְבַקֵּשׁ לִיתְּנָהּ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, לֵךְ וְהוֹדִיעָם
slides.label: Rav's teaching:
slides.text: One who gives a gift to another must inform him, derived from Exodus 31:13, 'to know that I am God who sanctifies you' — when God gave Israel the gift of Shabbat, He told Moses: 'I have a good gift in My treasure house and Shabbat is its name; go inform them.' From this Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel derived that one who gives bread to a child must inform the mother — originally by smearing the child with oil, later (once witchcraft was a concern) with the same food given. Rav Ḥisda so prized this teaching that he rewarded Rava bar Meḥasseya with two priestly gifts for reporting it in Rav's name.

slides.title: 👨‍👦 Three More Teachings from Rav
slides.subtitle: Reported by Rava bar Meḥasseya in the name of Rav Ḥama bar Gurya

steps.content: 1️⃣ Never favor one son over the others — Jacob gave Joseph an extra two sela of fine wool for his coat, his brothers grew jealous, and that chain of events led our ancestors down to Egypt
2️⃣ Always seek to settle in a newly-founded town — fewer years means fewer accumulated sins, as Lot called Zoar 'a small (i.e. recently settled) city' when he fled there (Genesis 19:20)
3️⃣ Rabbi Avin: the numerical value of נָא ('please') in Lot's plea 'let me escape there' is 51 — one year less than Sodom's 52, proving Zoar truly was newer

summary.principle: A person must prepare himself with reverence to stand before God in prayer without letting it displace Torah study, and this ethic of proper preparation and proper regard for others runs through the daf's teachings on courts, bathhouses, and gifts.

flowSteps.content: 🙏 'Prepare to greet your God' — belt and cloak customs before the Amida (Amos 4:12)
❓ Torah or prayer first? Rava rebukes lengthy prayer; R' Zeira rebukes cutting study short

columns.content: ⏰ Courts: a trial begins at the tallit or the plea; judges sit only until mealtime
🛁 Bathhouse: pray only in the outer, dressed room

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: A gift — like Shabbat itself — must be made known to the one receiving it

quiz.q: Which verse do the Sages cite as the reason one should prepare himself (e.g. with a belt or cloak) before praying?
o: Amos 4:12, 'Prepare to greet your God, Israel'
Deuteronomy 6:7, 'When you lie down and when you rise'
Psalms 41:4, 'God will support him on the bed of illness'
Leviticus 22:7, 'And the sun sets and it is purified'
quiz.e: The Gemara grounds the practice of dressing with dignity for prayer in Amos 4:12, 'Prepare to greet your God, Israel.'

quiz.q: How did Rava prepare himself to pray, and what did he say as he did so?
o: He donned expensive socks and cited 'prepare to greet your God'
He removed his cloak and clasped his hands, saying he stood 'like a slave before his master'
He wrapped himself in an elaborate garment
He stood without a belt to show submission
quiz.e: Rava removed his cloak and clasped his hands in extreme submission, comparing himself to a slave before his master — unlike Rava bar Rav Huna, who dressed elaborately.

quiz.q: What did Rabbi Zeira say about Rabbi Yirmeya, who hurried to end a Torah discussion in order to pray on time?
o: He praised him for his devotion to prayer
He applied to him the verse 'one who turns his ear from hearing Torah, his prayer too is an abomination'
He ruled that Rabbi Yirmeya need not have hurried at all
He said Torah study may always be interrupted for prayer without concern
quiz.e: Rabbi Zeira quoted Proverbs 28:9 against Rabbi Yirmeya for cutting Torah study short in order to pray.

quiz.q: According to Rav Ḥiyya bar Rav from Difti, what does 'the people stood over Moses from the morning until the evening' (Exodus 18:13) actually teach?
o: That Moses literally judged the people all day without pause
That a judge who renders one truthful judgment, even for a single hour, is considered a partner with God in Creation
That judges must fast while sitting in judgment
That court may never adjourn before nightfall
quiz.e: Since Moses also needed time for his own Torah study, the verse instead teaches that even one hour of true judgment makes a judge God's partner in Creation, linked by verbal analogy to Genesis 1:5.

quiz.q: Why, according to Rav, must one who gives a gift inform the recipient that he is giving it?
o: So the recipient can reciprocate appropriately
Derived from Exodus 31:13 — just as God informed Israel about the gift of Shabbat, a gift should be made known to its recipient
So the value of the gift can be assessed
Because an unannounced gift may later be reclaimed by the giver
quiz.e: Rav derived this from Exodus 31:13, noting that God told Moses to inform Israel about the gift of Shabbat — 'a good gift in My treasure house.'
